sections.h2: Who values and bills a house in Midland
sections.html:
In Midland County a single agency handles valuation and billing. That agency, the Midland Central Appraisal District, appraises every parcel and mails the statements. It works from 4631 Andrews Hwy and answers at 432-699-4991 on weekdays between 8 and 5.

Roughly 548,842 statements for the 2026 tax year went into the mail on October 23, 2026. If your parcel is across the line in Martin County, a different office appraises and bills it. Call the Martin County tax office in that case.

Think of four roles. The district sets the value. A review board hears disputes. Each taxing unit (city, school, county, college, hospital) picks its own budget and rate. A collector then multiplies and sends out the bill.

The City of Midland moved from $0.347999 per $100 in 2025 to $0.383092 in 2026, and the county, the college and the hospital all went up too. Midland ISD stayed flat at 0.841500.

sections.h2: What a late payment costs after January 31
sections.html:
A statement can be paid the day it arrives. Collection opens around October 1, and nothing extra is added until February 1. That morning the unpaid balance is hit with six percent in penalty and one percent in interest. The penalty grows by a point every month and levels off at twelve percent once July arrives. Interest never levels off.

  • A collection lawyer, if the unit has one under contract, can bill up to 20 percent more.
  • Seniors and disabled owners can pay in four pieces.
  • Delinquent accounts sometimes get payment plans stretching to 36 months, though only a residence homestead has a right to one.
  • Asking for the late charges to be waived takes a written request before day 181, and the tax itself must be paid within 21 days of finding out it was late.

Paying at the counter? Bring the account number from your statement and keep the receipt with your sale papers. Call ahead to learn which payment types the counter takes.

Midland ISD takes $140,000 off a homestead. The City of Midland has no general homestead amount, but it does help older owners with $8,000 for age 65 or older.

  • Age 65 or older: county $150,000, city $8,000, hospital $20,000, college $8,000, Midland ISD $60,000.
  • Disability: county $150,000 and Midland ISD $60,000.
  • You may claim the age exemption or the disability one but not both, and the age one tends to be worth more.
  • The county's optional homestead percentage is set at 3 percent with a $5,000 floor, though $0 is actually granted.
  • A disabled veteran receives $5,000, $7,500, $10,000 or $12,000 by disability bracket, and a 100 percent rating covers the full homesteadable value.

Exemptions belong to the person who owned on January 1, which means a buyer closing later in the year has to file fresh. If you forgot to file, the district takes a late homestead application for up to a year after the tax turns delinquent. Turning 65 this year? Apply any time before year end and the exemption covers the full year.

sections.h2: How to challenge a Midland value
sections.html:
The appraisal notice usually shows up in mid-April. A protest must be filed by May 15, or thirty days after you receive the notice when that gives you more time. Homestead notices are aimed at April 1, so check the mailbox early.

The notice describes the property, shows its value and exemptions, and estimates the tax. Values shift when comparable sales move or when a record is corrected for a measurement or a pool, so read the description line by line before you protest.

Still unhappy after the board rules? Court, binding arbitration and (for values over $1,000,000) the State Office of Administrative Hearings are open to you. The district looks at every property again at least once in three years, and a homestead's value can climb only ten percent a year once the exemption has been in place a full year.

Unpaid tax does not stop a sale. Closing staff request a payoff figure that includes tax, penalty, interest and any lawyer's fee. That number is deducted from your sale check. You do not have to pay anything up front unless you prefer to.

Do it in this order. Confirm whether the parcel sits in Midland or Martin County. Ask for the payoff in writing. Check whether a waiver request still fits inside the 181-day window. Last, pass the number to the closing office so your net-proceeds estimate is real.

Midland has grown fast. The city counted 132,524 residents in 2020 and now estimates 147,615 for July 2025, a gain of 11.1 percent. About 65.1 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, and a typical one is valued at $319,200. Those figures cover the whole city, and individual streets can run well above or below them, so the appraisal record for your own parcel matters more than any average.

sections.h2: What a Midland seller should do about property tax
sections.html:
Look up your account at the appraisal district before you list, since that one office both values the house and sends the bill. Each January 1 a lien attaches, and whoever owned the house that morning is responsible for the year's tax no matter when the deed moves.

  • Find out from the title company how the current year's tax will be divided between you and the buyer.
  • Your buyer should file a new homestead application, because the exemption now on file is yours.
  • On a delinquent account, request a payoff that shows penalty, interest and any attorney fee.
  • Inherited house? An heir whose name is on no recorded deed can still claim the exemption by giving the district an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

Because the city rate rose between 2025 and 2026 while the school rate held steady, a buyer comparing your 2026 statement with an older one will see a bigger city share. Keep both years' statements handy and point the buyer to the district's rate page. A cash sale removes the lender's appraisal and repair demands, but the tax payoff still gets settled at closing.

faqs.q: What is Midland's city tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The City of Midland's 2026 rate is $0.383092 per $100 of taxable value, up from $0.347999 in 2025. The school, county, college and hospital rates are added to it.

faqs.q: Who sends Midland County tax statements?
faqs.a: The Midland Central Appraisal District mails them. You can reach it at 4631 Andrews Hwy or 432-699-4991. For a Martin County parcel, call the Martin County tax office.

faqs.q: Does the City of Midland grant a regular homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No general amount, only $8,000 for owners 65 or older at the city level. Midland ISD exempts $140,000 of a homestead.

faqs.q: Is it too late to claim a homestead exemption I forgot?
faqs.a: Maybe not. Late applications are taken for a year after the bill goes delinquent, but nobody files it for you.

faqs.q: What does missing the January 31 date cost in Midland?
faqs.a: From February 1 the balance carries six percent penalty and one percent interest. Penalty hits twelve percent in July, interest keeps accruing, and a lawyer's fee of up to 20 percent may follow.
